issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a method addGuestStudents(int, String) (an int for the new guest students and a String reason), but the solution implements addGuestStudents(int) with only a single int parameter. This is a cross-artifact method-parameter mismatch: students following the problem/UML will implement/expect a two-parameter method (and tests may call it with two arguments), while the provided solution uses a one-parameter signature. This discrepancy can confuse students and cause failing tests or unclear expectations about how to provide the reason parameter.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the solution match the specification: change the solution's method signature to public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason) and update the implementation to add the new guest students (e.g. this.numberOfGuestStudents += numberOfNewGuestStudents). Optionally use or store the reason (or document that the reason is currently unused) so the implementation aligns with the problem statement and UML. Alternatively, if the reason parameter was not intended, update the problem statement and UML to reflect addGuestStudents(int) consistently.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML require a method addGuestStudents(int, String) (i.e., an int for the number of new guest students and a String reason). In the solution implementation, the method is defined as addGuestStudents(int) — it is missing the String reason parameter. The template contains a TODO for this method but no signature. This API mismatch (arity and parameter intent) creates a mapping confusion: students reading the problem expect to implement or use a two-parameter method (including a reason), but the provided solution uses only one parameter. This may cause confusion about how to handle the reason parameter and lead to failing signature-based tests or misaligned student implementations.
issues.suggested_fix: Align the implementation with the problem specification. Update the solution (and template) to implement the two-parameter signature: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason) { this.numberOfGuestStudents += numberOfNewGuestStudents; /* optionally log or store reason */ }. If the reason parameter is intentionally unused, at minimum accept it in the signature and document/handle it (e.g., log it). Alternatively, if the reason parameter is not intended, update the problem statement and UML to specify addGuestStudents(int) to remove the mismatch.
